subject: ISV integration: compatibility playbook & SDK handoff
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@mosaictools.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: ISV integration: compatibility playbook & next steps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and suite of fallback options you showed made a lot of sense for our use cases. MosaicTools builds a connector-first suite for enterprise knowledge workflows; several of our customers have asked for a certified Redwood adapter that wires into both LangChain and LlamaIndex workflows with tracing and cost-aware routing baked in.

High-level ask: we want a short, documented "compatibility playbook" and a lightweight SDK handoff so our engineers can ship an officially supported adapter. Specifically, we'll need:
- SDK hooks for model selection and fallback variants (LangChain & LlamaIndex)
- Minimal tracing instrumentation to correlate requests in our observability (OpenTelemetry traces)
- A compatibility matrix (runtime versions, tokenizer parity, quantization caveats)

Would Redwood be open to a joint "compatibility certification" process (guide + matrix + badge)? We can fund a small professional services retainer with ConsultLytics to speed up the integration.

Appreciate any pointers to an internal contact and your suggested sequencing.

Best,
Samir
Co-founder, MosaicTools

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and for proposing a joint process. We’re interested.

Quick plan proposal from our side:
1) Discovery call (this week) to align success criteria and scope (who owns each matrix row)
2) Technical spike (Redwood + Mosaic) to validate LangChain & LlamaIndex adapters and tracing surface area (2 weeks)
3) Deliverables: compatibility matrix, SDK checklist, short integration test harness, and an optional co-branded badge

I’m looping in Karthik (runtime/SDK lead) and Marissa (partnerships/ISV ops) to own technical and program coordination. Diego from Solutions will join for initial scoping on customer templates.

Samir — can you share a short list of Mosaic's prioritized customers and any hard constraints (on-prem only, telemetry requirements, PII redaction needs)? Also: are you OK with ConsultLytics as the PS partner?

I’ll propose times for a 30-min sync.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of ISV Alliances, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 13:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ISV integration: compatibility playbook & next steps

Adding some technical guardrails and open questions so the discovery can be productive: 

What we should validate in the spike:
- LangChain: adapter pattern (LLMChain vs Agent patterns). Ensure our streaming + function-calling semantics are mapped to LangChain's callback/stream interfaces.
- LlamaIndex: make sure docstore/embedding shims maintain deterministic chunking and embedding params; note: our quantized runtime variants (int8/4-bit) can introduce minor output variance — include "quantization notes" in the matrix.
- Tracing: propose OpenTelemetry span tags: redwood.request_id, model_variant, batch_size, route_policy. We'll want a sample set where both sides can join traces.
- Telemetry: ensure we can export summarized cost and latency per-token to Mosaic's observability; decide on sampling strategy (1% vs 10% for high-QPS flows).

Blocking compatibility items to capture in the matrix:
- Tokenization parity across LLM families
- Max sequence and chunking behavior
- Behavior differences with prefix caching enabled
- Fallback semantics: how model_variant substitution is surfaced to adapters

I'll attach a first-pass compatibility matrix template and a short SDK checklist we use internally. If Mosaic can run the spike in a staging account, we can complete the matrix faster.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
